title: Service boundaries and routing contracts (v0)
content:
Purpose and scope
---
This is a working doc to capture proposed service boundaries and routing contracts for the control plane components that coordinate inference traffic across regions and capacity tiers. Focus areas: API gateway responsibilities, orchestration/control-plane domain, runtime adapter contracts (communication with serving runtime), and multi-region routing policies.

This is intentionally light on formal diagrams (we'll add a Visio/diagrams PR), mostly notes and actionable items for the next architecture review.

High-level goals
- Keep the control plane thin: orchestration decisions and metadata vs per-request data path kept in the data plane.
- Make routing policy declarative and pluggable so product teams can choose latency/cost/affinity policies without changing runtime.
- Clear ownership boundaries so teams can iterate independently: platform-networking (API gateway), control-plane-orchestrator (policy, rollouts), serving-runtime (runtime adapters + connectors).
- Strong backward-compatible contracts: versioned RPC/HTTP schemas and negotiated feature flags.

Service boundaries (proposed)
1) API Gateway (team: platform-networking)
   - Responsibilities:
     - Customer-facing ingress for hosted API and Dedicated ingress proxying.
     - Edge authentication, rate-limiting, ingress-level quota enforcement.
     - Route to control-plane orchestration endpoints or directly to data-plane (runtime) when short-circuiting is enabled.
   - Contracts:
     - Exposes unified REST/HTTP gRPC endpoints documented in the API spec.
     - Mutually agreed header set for routing metadata: x-rw-customer-id, x-rw-priority-tier, x-rw-request-origin, x-rw-request-trace.
     - Authentication: bearer token + optional mTLS for Dedicated/Private.
   - Operational notes:
     - Gateway must be region-aware; default routing prefers same-region control plane but can fallback to global.
     - Health-check surface: /healthz/gateway and /healthz/upstream (control-plane and runtime).

2) Control-plane Orchestrator (team: control-plane-orchestrator)
   - Responsibilities:
     - Central policy engine: routing decision, canary/rollout coordination, capacity-aware placement decisions.
     - Maintain cluster state and short-lived allocation leases for runtime adapters.
     - Provide the routing contract service (routing-decider API) used by gateway and regional agents.
   - Contracts:
     - routing-decider API (gRPC, v1beta): accept routing query with metadata and return target endpoint(s), reason, and fallback plan.
     - Events stream (Kafka): changes to placement, model-version pinning, region-degradation alerts.
     - TTL semantics: returned endpoints are valid for N seconds (TTL) and include a version token for optimistic concurrency.
   - Ownership notes:
     - Orchestrator owns business logic for historical fallbacks (e.g. prefer quantized variant if full-precision unavailable).
     - Does NOT own per-request retry logic; it can recommend retries but gatekeeping & retry semantics reside in gateway/runtime.

3) Regional Agents and Runtime Adapters (team: serving-runtime)
   - Responsibilities:
     - Execute inference workloads, manage GPU pools, handle model loading/unloading, maintain KV cache.
     - Expose runtime-adapter endpoints that accept tokenized requests or encoder payloads depending on contract.
     - Implement local health checks and admission control (reject when memory pressure high).
   - Contracts:
     - adapter-control API (HTTP+gRPC hybrid): model load/unload, status, metrics, and liveness probes.
     - inference-call API: should support streaming tokens, function-calling framing, and a concise error model (retryable vs terminal).
     - Versioning: adapters must support adapter-protocol v1 and v2 compatibility headers.
   - Operational notes:
     - Adapters are region-bound; they register to the control-plane Orchestrator via a heartbeat + announce (includes numeric capacity).
     - Local routing (within region) should prefer warmed KV cache hosts for low-latency requests.

Routing policy primitives (declarative)
- priority: latency | cost | affinity | regulatory
- region_affinity: prefer_same_region | prefer_nearest | require_region:<region-code>
- fallbacks: list of model variants (e.g. full_float_70b -> q4_70b -> small-13b)
- capacity_threshold: percentage of available capacity to consider before routing elsewhere
- customer_tier_overrides: e.g., enterprise customers bypass cost-first policies

Examples
- Low-latency user-facing chat (production): priority=latency, region_affinity=prefer_same_region, fallbacks=[full -> q4], capacity_threshold=0.1
- Background embedding batch job: priority=cost, region_affinity=prefer_nearest, fallbacks=[q4_only], capacity_threshold=0.0

Multi-region considerations
- Control-plane topology:
  - Active-active control plane instances in 3 regions (us-west, eu-central, ap-southeast).
  - Global orchestration cluster holds eventual consistency metadata; regional read-optimised caches for low-latency reads.
- Data residency:
  - Orchestrator exposes region pins for customer projects. If a customer requires EU-only, routing-decider must filter endpoints accordingly.
- Network fallbacks:
  - If regional runtime adapters become unreachable, orchestrator returns fallback endpoints in other regions with 'cross-region' tag and a higher cost estimate.
- Leader responsibilities:
  - No single leader for routing decisions. Use a constrained consensus for allocations (raft clusters per-control-shard) and allow region-local decisions for ephemeral placements.

Operational SLOs and telemetry
- SLOs (control plane): routing-decider median latency <20ms, 99th <100ms.
- SLOs (gateway): cold-start to routing-decision <10ms added. Token path end-to-end p50 <120ms for warm KV hits.
- Metrics to emit: routing_decisions_total{policy}, fallback_count, cross_region_routed_total, adapter_rejection_rate, model_load_time_seconds.
- Logging: include policy_id and decision_token on every routed request for traceability.

Contracts and versioning strategy
- Semantic versioning for APIs (major.minor): breaking changes bump major.
- Backward compatibility: gateway and runtime adapters must negotiate minimum supported minor.
- Feature flags: new routing features shipped behind server-side flags keyed by team and environment.

Failure modes and graceful degradation
- If orchestrator unavailable: gateway falls back to cached routing table for TTL window; if cache stale, route to a best-effort pool with lower capacity guarantees.
- If adapter rejects due to OOM: return explicit error with code ADAPTER_REJECT_OOM and a suggested fallback model variant.
- If region partition: mark region degraded and shift stateful rollouts to other regions after agreement (auto if agreed policy = true).

Open questions / trade-offs
- How much routing policy logic belongs in the gateway vs orchestrator? Gateway-local fast-path + orchestrator-decision for complex cases seems desirable, but increases duplication. Need perf data.
- Should the adapter-level inference-call carry full high-level routing metadata (policy name) or just a decision token? Passing full metadata helps observability but increases payloads.
- Cross-region data egress costs: should policy include cost-estimates to be evaluated in real-time or offline heuristics?

Next actions (short-term)
- [ ] Prototype routing-decider gRPC with TTL semantics (Connor). Jira: JIRA-PLAT-4821
- [ ] Define exact header set and immutability rules for gateway <-> orchestrator (Maya).
- [ ] Add adapter-protocol v2 doc in repo and backwards test harness (Lina). PR: github.com/redwood-inference/control-plane/pull/319
- [ ] Perf microbenchmarks: cached routing lookup latency vs full gRPC call (ownership: eng-sre).

Notes to reviewers
- This is deliberately pragmatic — we want to iterate on contracts quickly. Please add comments inline or Slack #platform-arch. For the architecture review, I'll produce a small sequence diagram and a compact contract YAML for review.

Appendix (sketches to convert to diagram)
- Sequence: client -> gateway -> (cached routing? yes) -> regional agent adapter -> runtime
- Sequence fallback: client -> gateway -> orchestrator -> choose cross-region adapter -> gateway proxies to remote region

End.
